summary: Meter allocation problems (flow with no deal in OSS or CPR, POPS feeding zero volumes to Sitara, desk-to-desk variances, counterparties chasing payment) are found one meter at a time. Each one becomes its own email to Daren Farmer or volume management and can sit unanswered for days or weeks. A read-only exception report, run after each allocation, would compare measured flow, POPS confirmed and allocated volumes and Sitara/OSS deals, and give each meter a structured ticket with the evidence already attached. It saves about $62/month ($744/year) of handling, but most of its value is that big UA4 and P&L problems get caught the day they appear.

current_workflow.step: A settlements or accounting analyst working a UA4 or allocation exception finds a meter with flow but no matching deal. They check OSS, CPR and MIPs measurement statements by hand.
The analyst emails the logistics desk (usually Daren Farmer) to ask whether a deal exists, whether a CPR deal failed to feed OSS, or how a short or under-pulled nomination should be handled.

Volume management or scheduling spots wrong data in POPS by chance while reviewing imbalances: missing BAV feeds, zero volumes fed back to Sitara, delivery noms at receipt meters, confirmations on days the deal does not cover. They then escalate by email.
Open items pile up and are chased with follow-ups, kept on a hand-maintained outstanding-issues list, or forwarded between managers until someone checks the allocation.

The fix is coordinated by hand across several people: zero confirmed noms, change the allocation method, reallocate, verify BAV adjustments with Settlements, update facilities, or have a deal extended or set up.

solution.approach: A read-only reconciliation job runs after each POPS allocation and again at month-end. For every meter and day it pulls measured volume (MIPs measurement statements), POPS confirmed noms and allocated volumes, and the Sitara/OSS deals and their valid dates. It applies a fixed set of rules: flow with no deal, deal with no flow, zero or missing feed from POPS to Sitara, a delivery nom at a receipt meter, a confirmation outside the deal's date range, a nomination not pulled, and allocated vs measured differences beyond a tolerance. Each rule hit becomes an exception row. The row carries the meter, period, volumes from each source, the prior month for context, and a suggested owner (logistics desk, volume management, settlements). Exceptions go to one shared queue with status and age, replacing ad hoc emails and the hand-kept outstanding-issues list. Owners still decide the fix, and their resolution note is saved with the row.
solution.trigger: Completion of the daily POPS allocation run, plus a scheduled month-end run before UA4 close
inputs: MIPs measurement statement volumes by meter and day
POPS confirmed nominations, allocation method and allocated volumes
Sitara deal tickets (meter, counterparty, valid dates, volume)
OSS and CPR deal records for the same meters and periods
meter attributes (receipt vs delivery, allocatable flag)
outputs: daily exception list by meter for volume management and the logistics desk
month-end UA4 exception summary for settlements and accounting managers
aging report of open exceptions, replacing the manual interdesk/interconnect outstanding list
per-exception evidence pack the analyst can forward to the counterparty or pipeline
components: extracts from POPS, Sitara, OSS, CPR and MIPs into a staging table
rule-based variance engine with per-rule tolerances
exception queue with owner, status, age and resolution note
routing table mapping meters and rule types to owners

implementation_steps: Inventory the past year of exception emails and agree the rule list and tolerances with volume management, logistics and settlements.
Arrange read-only extracts from POPS, Sitara, OSS, CPR and MIPs, keyed by meter number and gas day.
Build the staging table and the meter and deal matching logic. Handle CPR-to-OSS feed lag by comparing both.
Implement the rules one at a time, starting with flow-with-no-deal and zero POPS-to-Sitara feed, and test them against known historical cases (e.g. meters 1441, 986782, 984132).
Build the exception queue and routing table, with owners named by volume management.
Run in parallel with the current email process for one month-end, and tune tolerances to remove noise.
Switch the month-end UA4 review and the outstanding-issues list over to the queue, and ask analysts to file new exceptions there rather than by email.
stays_manual: Deciding which volume is correct when sources disagree (e.g. pipeline vs HPL Measurement custody questions), because it depends on contracts and custody transfer.
Creating, extending or moving deals in Sitara and reallocating meters in POPS, because these change P&L and are owned by logistics and volume management.
Legal or commercial calls such as whether gas is bought as wellhead, or which book a sale belongs in.
Talking to counterparties and pipelines (Transco, Exxon, Pennzoil and others) to settle imbalances.
risks: The evidence does not say what extracts or interfaces POPS, OSS, CPR and MIPs offer. If no extract exists, effort could grow from M to L, so confirm data access first.
Meter numbers appear in different formats across messages (e.g. 98-9699, 986892, 0980439), and meters get replaced. A meter cross-reference must be maintained or matches will be missed.
Loose tolerances will flood analysts with noise, and tight ones will miss material UA4 items. Tune them during the parallel run.

Measured savings are small ($62/month at $85/hour), so the funding case rests on catching large feed failures early, like the 500,000 MMBtu POPS imbalance. That benefit is not priced in these figures.
Exceptions without a clear owner will still stall. The routing table needs a named owner and an escalation path for each rule.
success_metric: Number of meters with measured flow but no matching Sitara/OSS deal still open at month-end UA4 close, and median age of open allocation exceptions
